transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Tachyon Head of ML), Omar Bennett (Tachyon Platform Eng), Clara Nguyen (Tachyon CTO)

Summary (auto):
Quick discovery focused on latency and throughput requirements for customer-facing streaming generation and batch reranking. Discussed p95 targets, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming token/sec benchmarks, and tradeoffs between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployment models. Agreed next steps around benchmarking and dedicated sizing.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, i'll hand over to marco in a sec who is our se but first quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: hi i'm priya, head of ml at tachyon media, we do realtime captions and headline generation for live sports, so latency is a big deal for us.
[00:21] Omar: omer — platform eng, i'll own infra questions and compliance bits
[00:25] Clara: clara here, cto, focused on cost and uptime SLA
[00:30] Marco: hi folks, marco here — i'll focus on the throughput/latency tradeoffs and do some technical Qs as we go
[00:40] Lena: great, high level, are you exploring hosted vs dedicated vs private? what's the driving factor — latency, cost, data residency?
[00:51] Priya: latency and predictability mostly. hosted is attractive for speed to market but we worry about noisy neighbors and p95 spikes during peak games. we target p95 end-to-end generation under 800ms for 128 token prompts, ideally 500ms.
[01:08] Omar: concurrency is also huge — we see spikes to 800 concurrent sessions during big events, average 250 concurrent. some streaming outputs vs some full-response use cases.
[01:22] Marco: ok good detail. couple clarifying q's: by 'end-to-end' do you mean from request accept to first token or full response?
[01:30] Priya: first token is most critical for UX, but full response p95 we'd like under 1.5s for the short ones. for streaming we want first byte p95 under 300-400ms ideally.
[01:42] Marco: got it. what models are you evaluating? smaller Llama-family or larger open models?
[01:48] Priya: currently prototyping with a 13B quantized model for generation and a 7B for reranking, but we may move to a 70B variant for quality soon for some premium feeds.
[01:58] Marco: that helps. tradeoffs: hosted can meet p95 for 13B if you accept some concurrency-based variance. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation — you'd size pools for peak concurrency and get consistent p95. Private/VPC buys you network control and KMS integration but adds ops overhead.
[02:16] Lena: also note our streaming plumbing — we support streaming with low-latency first-token prioritization and prefix cache which helps multi-request use cases.
[02:26] Clara: prefix cache? can you explain briefly?
[02:29] Marco: yeah, so if many requests share the same prompt prefix (e.g., event metadata), our runtime caches the KV cache for that prefix and reuses it, which reduces per-token compute and helps both p95 and throughput. not magic but helps a lot in broadcast-like prompt patterns.
[02:45] Omar: interesting. for our live captions we have lots of shared context, that could save a lot. how do you handle batching vs latency tradeoff?
[02:53] Marco: our scheduler does continuous batching with latency-aware cutoffs. so if you need sub-300ms p95 first token we'll prioritize small batches and lower batching windows; that costs more tokens/sec per GPU. if you relax p95 you get larger batches and better token/sec efficiency.
[03:09] Priya: what's typical token/sec per GPU for a 13B quantized profile? both for streaming and non-streaming.
[03:17] Marco: approximate numbers — on an rtx-type fleet equivalent, you might see 800-1,200 tokens/sec peak for a 13B quantized model with decent batching; for 70B it's more like 200-400 tokens/sec unless heavily quantized and tuned. streaming first-token latency for 13B can be sub-250ms with Dedicated and proper warm cache.
[03:36] Priya: those ranges are helpful; our current SLO targets for first token are 300ms p95 during events, but average day is more lenient. cost is another axis: we don't want dedicated capacity wasted off-peak. how does redwood help with burst and autoscaling?
[03:50] Marco: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. you can reserve baseline capacity for predictable load and allow bursts to hosted pool or spare capacity that we run when needed. there's also routing policies that prefer cheaper models if load is constrained.
[04:06] Clara: what about benchmarking — we want to run token/sec benchmarks with our actual prompts and measure p95 at different concurrencies. can you run that or do we run?
[04:15] Marco: we can run it if you provide the prompt histogram and sample payloads. we typically run a synthetic driver that replays your mix at target concurrencies and measure p95 first-token and full-response times, plus token/sec achieved per instance.
[04:27] Omar: do you support streaming TLS streaming and do logs contain latency breakdowns per token?
[04:32] Marco: yes streaming over TLS, and Console has per-request token-level timing breakdowns, KV cache hits, batching windows, and GPU utilization. we'll share a sample benchmark report.
[04:44] Priya: for the 70B consideration — you mentioned 200-400 tokens/sec — at 400 we'd still be falling short during peak. could we do sharding or hybrid models? like 13B for majority and 70B for premium?
[04:56] Marco: absolutely, hybrid routing is a common pattern. you can route base traffic to 13B and send a subset to 70B. Redwood's routing policies support percent-based rollouts and fallback to smaller models if 70B is saturated.
[05:10] Lena: quick q on security — what about data retention / KMS / SOC2?
[05:15] Marco: Hosted keeps short retention by default but not ideal for regulated PII unless you enable dedicated or private. Dedicated gives tenant isolation and we support customer-managed keys for payload encryption at rest. Private gives full control of control-plane and network. SOC2 is available, we'll share the package.
[05:28] Priya: we will need SOC2 + audit logs + SSO (SAML). that's non-negotiable for some partners.
[05:33] Lena: noted. we'll attach compliance docs.
[05:37] Omar: back to the benchmark — what does your benchmarking tool measure? p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU util, batching windows?
[05:45] Marco: yes all of those. we also capture distribution of sequence lengths, prefix cache hit rate, and cold vs warm latencies. the benchmark will simulate warm state by preloading KV caches where appropriate.
[05:56] Priya: about p95 targets: our product team expects under 300ms first-token when model is 13B and cached for common prompts. is that realistic?
[06:04] Marco: for 13B with dedicated warm KV cache and small batching yes it's realistic on modern GPUs; on hosted shared pools you might see higher variance. I'd put a high confidence on sub-300ms first-token with Dedicated tuned for your workload.
[06:18] Clara: do you have an example sizing calc? like if we have 800 concurrent during peak, and each session averages 2 requests per minute with 128 tokens, how many dedicated GPUs do we need?
[06:30] Marco: rough calc: if each GPU does 1,000 tokens/sec sustained for your 13B profile, that's 60k tokens/minute. with 800 concurrent and say each request is 128 tokens and 2 req/min that's 800 * 128 * 2 = 204,800 tokens/min, so you'd need around 4 GPUs sustained (204,800 / 60,000 = ~3.4) but you'd add headroom for spikes and lower batching efficiency: typically multiply by 1.5-2 => 6-8 GPUs. that aligns with baseline reserved capacity plus burst.
[07:01] Priya: that math helps. can we get a worked example in the sizing sheet?
[07:05] Lena: yes we'll include that.
[07:07] Omar: streaming specifics: could you guarantee ordering of tokens for streaming consumers and partial retries? we have idempotency constraints.
[07:15] Marco: yes streaming is ordered, and we provide tokens offsets. for retries we recommend client-side idempotency keys; the runtime supports best-effort dedupe at the API layer but it's safer to rely on idempotency keys.
[07:28] Priya: in practical terms what kind of p95 variance do you see during big events with hosted?
[07:33] Marco: hosted can spike; we've seen p95 double during intense spikes if you're on shared pools and your prefix cache is cold. Dedicated smooths that out. Also routing to nearby region helps.
[07:45] Clara: regioning question — we have users in EU and US, do you support multi-region deployment with active-active?
[07:52] Marco: yes we support region routing policies and active-active with replicated models. there's additional cost for cross-region replication for model weights and you need to size per-region.
[08:03] Priya: ok, re benchmarks — what exact artifacts should we send you to run the synthetic driver?
[08:09] Marco: ideally: 1) prompt histogram (percentiles of token lengths), 2) representative sample of prompts (200-500), 3) expected concurrency curve (minute-level for a typical event), 4) which models to test and any special decoding settings (top-p, temp, streaming enabled).
[08:26] Priya: we'll collect that.
[08:29] Lena: high level pricing q — if we do dedicated reserved plus burst to hosted, how is that priced?
[08:35] Marco: dedicated is commit-based monthly/annual; burst to hosted is pay-as-you-go. we can provide a blended cost model in the sizing doc.
[08:45] Omar: question about token accounting: do you charge for partial tokens during streaming?
[08:50] Lena: we charge per token generated, streaming or not — no double-billing. there is a small rounding approach for partial tokens but it's the same accounting.
[08:59] Priya: one more: for the large 70B option, would quantization and kernel selection meaningfully improve throughput or is it diminishing returns?
[09:08] Marco: quantization helps a lot depending on model architecture; combined with kernel selection and compilation we can get 2-3x improvements in throughput for some 70B variants, but it's model dependent. we'll include model-specific performance profiles for the models you plan to test.
[09:24] Clara: SLA question — what uptime and p95 SLOs do you offer for Dedicated?
[09:29] Lena: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets in enterprise contracts; we'll surface the specifics in the contract and they depend on the commit level and region redundancy.
[09:39] Priya: ok great. are there any gotchas with prefix cache and privacy? like if shared cache could leak prompts?
[09:45] Marco: no, caches are per-tenant for dedicated/private. for hosted we use sharding and don't expose tenant data across other tenants; we can provide the security architecture doc.
[09:56] Omar: do you support customer KMS for encrypted model weights in private?
[10:00] Marco: yes for Private we support customer-managed keys for storage and you can integrate with HSM for additional control; we'll share integration notes.
[10:09] Priya: timeline — we want a pilot before the next big season in 6 weeks, is that feasible?
[10:14] Lena: feasible if we get the prompt histogram and run the benchmarks this week. pilot could be Hosted first for quick win and then Dedicated pilot for peak smoothing.
[10:24] Marco: technical note — to simulate warm-state we need to pre-run common prefixes to populate KV cache in the benchmark driver, otherwise numbers will understate production performance.
[10:36] Priya: makes sense.
[10:38] Marco: any compliance blockers?
[10:40] Omar: SOC2 coverage and SSO — otherwise good.
[10:43] Lena: we'll attach SOC2 and SSO docs in follow-up.
[10:47] Priya: can you also include a sample benchmark report for a 13B workload with 250/800 concurrencies? both numbers are useful (avg vs peak).
[10:56] Marco: yes we'll run both and show p50/p95/p99 and token/sec and GPU util.
[11:03] Clara: can you include suggested model mix and routing policy for hybrid approach?
[11:08] Marco: yes, we'll propose a percent-based split and fallback rules.
[11:12] Lena: ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[11:16] Lena: action items — lena send pricing and sizing, marco run benchmarks, priya send prompts/histogram, omar confirm compliance items. we'll aim to reconvene after benchmarks.
[11:27] Priya: sounds good, thanks all.
[11:29] Clara: thanks.
[11:30] Marco: thanks everyone, will follow up with timelines.

(end of call)
